<aside class="blog-tldr not-prose"><div class="blog-tldr__label">TL;DR</div><div class="blog-tldr__body">
- Mistakes are operational, not policy
- Post-acute partners get overlooked
- Data arrives too late to act
- Track strategy needs ownership
</div></aside>

The **CMS TEAM model** has been live since January 1, 2026, and early reporting reveals recurring implementation gaps.

## Gap 1: Underinvesting in episode data

Because claims data lags roughly six months, hospitals relying on retrospective reporting discover problems too late to intervene. Documentation is a related weak spot: per Optum Advisory, "analysis of one facility found that two-thirds of episodes had zero HCCs coded" — under-documented comorbidities produce lower target prices that don’t reflect true episode cost.

## Gap 2: Treating the PCP referral as an afterthought

HFMA reporting quotes hospital leaders that the mandatory primary-care referral has been "more challenging than a lot of people thought," with confusion over what counts as a referral, the timeline, and which clinicians qualify — a problem compounded when patients report no PCP.

## Gap 3: Mis-timing patient attribution

HFMA reporting notes the lack of a precise crosswalk between clinical workflows and DRG-based billing constructs makes it hard to identify TEAM patients early enough to begin care navigation and discharge planning.

## Gap 4: Assuming 2026 buys time

An upside-only Performance Year 1 lulls some hospitals into delay, but two-sided risk begins in 2027 and the required infrastructure takes months to build.

## Gap 5: Ignoring safety-net exposure

Peer-reviewed research shows safety-net hospitals were disproportionately penalized under CJR because of lower, harder-to-meet spending targets; the same structural risk exists under TEAM.

## Gap 6: Underweighting quality

The Composite Quality Score can flip a projected savings into a repayment — up to a 15% swing on negative reconciliation amounts.

## How should hospitals correct course?

Invest in real-time data, operationalize the PCP referral, solve attribution early, act in 2026 rather than waiting, and treat quality as a financial lever — not a compliance checkbox.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is CMS TEAM currently live?

Yes. CMS TEAM has been live since January 1, 2026.

### What's the biggest data gap hospitals face under CMS TEAM?

Reliance on lagging claims data, which trails roughly six months, leaving hospitals unable to intervene on episodes in real time.

### Why has the CMS TEAM PCP referral requirement been difficult?

Hospital leaders report ambiguity over what counts as a qualifying referral, the required timeline, and which clinicians satisfy the requirement — compounded when patients report having no primary care provider.

### Does the upside-only design of Performance Year 1 buy hospitals time?

No. Two-sided financial risk begins in 2027, and the infrastructure needed to manage it takes months to build — delaying preparation in 2026 is a common and costly mistake.

### Are safety-net hospitals at higher risk under CMS TEAM?

Research on the predecessor CJR model suggests yes — safety-net hospitals were disproportionately penalized because of lower, harder-to-meet spending targets, a structural risk that carries into TEAM.
